Since the first version

What changed after your corrections

This is what we changed from what you told us in the second conversation. Please tell us if we understood anything wrongly.

Proto sample

Before

The merchant secures the fabric and briefs the sample team at the same moment, and checks the first sample with the technical team.

Now

The merchant follows the BOM and the board, secures fabric and trims, raises a sample request to the sample room and chases the trims. The sample room makes the pattern and a mock sample at once. When the right fabric arrives, the merchant and sample team evaluate it together, then the final proto sample is made.

LA pieces

Before

One piece per colour.

Now

2 pieces for LA, 1 for the critical fit and 4 to 5 for development testing. Whether this is per colour or per style is one of the questions below.

Critical fit

Before

A separate stage after LA.

Now

Part of the LA stage, together with the development samples.

Proto meeting

Before

Technical managers and pattern makers shown in the technical lane.

Now

The meeting sits with the merchant, so the technical box is removed.

Block pattern

Before

The brand sends a block pattern.

Now

The block pattern information sits in the brand's PLM, and the team pulls it from there.

Scope

Before

Ended at selection and placement.

Now

Adds carry-over styles, which skip the proto, and open issue samples, which return after selection and repeat the LA process.

Also added from your second conversation

  • The brand's board is shared and used live. It can't be exported and the brand controls who logs in, so details are copied by hand.
  • The merchant creates the BOM as well. Fabric, trim and pattern information is the same across proto, LA and the PRR.
  • Development testing is a separate path. Its results link to the PRR when they come, with no waiting.
  • No system shows which fabrics and trims are available. The closest colour comes from the colour book.
